# Privacy policy

> **Draft for counsel review.** Prepared 2026-10-30 from the code and configuration of Align. It is not legal advice
> and is not yet in force. The bracketed placeholders are filled in when it is published.

This policy explains what personal data Align collects, why, how long it is kept, who else handles it, and the
choices and rights you have. "Align", "we" and "us" mean [LEGAL ENTITY]. Write to us at
[PRIVACY CONTACT EMAIL].

<!-- Counsel: decide whether an EU (GDPR Art. 27) or UK representative is needed, and add it here. -->

## Our two roles

- **Controller** for your account, for this website and its sign-in, for the request-access form, for security and
  abuse prevention, and for product events. We decide why and how that data is used, and this policy covers it.
- **Processor** for workspace data: the goals, members, teams, change requests, shared sessions and everything else
  people put in a workspace. We process it on behalf of the organization the workspace belongs to (our customer),
  under our agreement with them and the [data processing agreement](dpa.md). That organization's own privacy notice
  governs it; we help them answer requests about it.
- **Local mode.** Align can run on your own computer instead of on our servers. Then everything stays on your
  computer, and we receive none of it.

## What we collect

| Data | What it is | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account | Your email address and name; if you sign in with Google or GitHub, the provider's account id, your profile picture address and the tokens the provider issued at sign-in (kept by our sign-in software, the access and refresh tokens encrypted; we do not use them afterwards). If you sign in with an email code and give no name, your name starts as the part of your email before the @ | You, Google or GitHub <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts; Better Auth ba_user, ba_account --> |
| Passkeys | Each passkey's public key, its name, when it was added and when it was last used, and whether you dismissed the "add a passkey" prompt | You <!-- lib/v2/account.ts --> |
| Sign-in sessions | A session token in a cookie and, on our servers, your IP address and browser's user agent | Your browser <!-- docs/RETENTION.md --> |
| Email sign-in codes | A hash of each code, for 5 minutes | Us <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts --> |
| Devices | The name you give a computer that runs the `align` agent, its public key, when it was last seen, and hashes of its tokens | You <!-- lib/v2/devices.ts --> |
| Connected AI apps | For each app you connect: its name and return address as it gives them, the workspace, when you connected it and last used it, a hash of its refresh token, and the scopes you granted | You and the app <!-- lib/oauth/grants.ts --> |
| Workspace data (we are processor) | Workspace name, members and their roles, teams, invites (the invitee's email), goals and their versions, alignments, change requests with their notes and decisions, evidence links on change requests, labelled self-reported or agent-reported, and goal snapshots Align computes, directives, and the audit log | People in the workspace <!-- lib/v2/db.ts --> |
| Shared sessions (we are processor) | For each agent session a person chooses to share: which agent it was (Claude Code or Codex), a hashed repository key, an optional repository alias, times, state, the goal it works toward, and token usage with estimated cost | The `align` agent on the person's computer <!-- docs/RETENTION.md --> |
| Work signals (we are processor) | For 24 hours: hashes of files a shared session touched, and, only if the person turns on "share work signals", file paths and short text such as a task or commit title | The `align` agent <!-- lib/v2/activity.ts --> |
| Access requests | Email, name, company, team size, what you want to use Align for, and your interest (try or evaluate) | You, on the request-access form <!-- app/app/request-access/view.tsx --> |
| Creation codes | A keyed hash of each code, the email it is for, its dates, and the workspace it created | Us <!-- lib/v2/db.ts v2_creation_codes --> |
| Abuse prevention | Rate-limit counters keyed by a keyed hash of an email address or network address; when the bot check is on, what Cloudflare Turnstile collects in your browser and your IP address | Your browser <!-- lib/v2/limits.ts; lib/v2/captcha.ts --> |
| Product events | An event name (such as "workspace created" or "first session shared"), the workspace, a keyed hash that stands for the person, the time, and a few allowlisted properties such as the interest chosen on the request form. Never an email, name, title, address or token | Our server |
| Messages we send | Sign-in codes and creation codes, sent to your email address | Us |

**What we never collect on our servers:** the prompts you or your colleagues write to coding agents, the agents'
replies and tool output, your code and file contents, or a session's title. **Cookies:** only the ones needed to
sign in: your session cookie and short-lived cookies set during a Google, GitHub or passkey sign-in. We use no
analytics, advertising or tracking cookies and no third-party analytics.

## Why we use it, and our legal bases

| Purpose | Data | Legal basis (EU and UK GDPR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create your account, sign you in, keep you signed in | Account, passkeys, sessions, codes, devices | Contract |
| Provide workspaces to our customers | Workspace data, shared sessions, work signals, connected apps | Contract with our customer (as processor, on their instructions) |
| Answer a request for access and send a creation code | Access requests, creation codes | Steps before a contract, at your request; legitimate interests in choosing whom to onboard |
| Keep Align secure and stop abuse | Sessions (IP address, user agent), rate-limit counters, the bot check, the audit log | Legitimate interests in security, and the customer's interest in an audit trail |
| Understand whether people get value from Align, in aggregate | Product events, which hold no content and no direct identifiers | Legitimate interests in improving the product |
| Meet legal obligations | Any of the above, as required | Legal obligation |

We do not sell personal data, share it for advertising, or use it to train AI models. Align's server sends no data to
any AI model provider.

## Who else handles it

- **Our subprocessors**: Fly.io (hosting), our email provider (Resend in the default configuration) and, when the bot
  check is on, Cloudflare Turnstile. See the [subprocessor list](subprocessors.md).
- **Google and GitHub**, if you choose to sign in with them.
- **People in your workspace**, according to their role and the visibility of each goal.
- **AI apps you connect**, which read one workspace as you, with your permissions. You choose them, and their makers
  handle what they read under their own terms.
- **Authorities**, when the law requires it, and a successor if [LEGAL ENTITY] is merged or sold, under this policy.

## How long we keep it

Our full retention schedule is published at [RETENTION.md](../RETENTION.md) and applied by a daily job. In short:

- Sign-in sessions: 7 days from last use, never more than 30 days from sign-in. Email codes: 5 minutes.
- Shared session details: 13 months after the session ends, then only totals with no person attached.
- Work signals: 24 hours.
- Workspace audit log: 1 year.
- People who leave a workspace: shown as "Former member" there after 30 days.
- A deleted workspace: restorable for 30 days, then deleted, and gone from our backups within 38 days.
- Access requests: deleted 13 months after we approve or decline them, or 13 months after they were made if still
  pending.
- Product events: 13 months.
- Your account: until you delete it.
- Backups: daily snapshots of our database, each kept 7 days.

## Your rights

You can ask us for a copy of your personal data, to correct it, to delete it, to restrict or object to its use, and
to receive it in a portable form; where we rely on consent, you can withdraw it. You can also complain to your data
protection authority.

- **Delete your account yourself** at `/app/account` (it asks you to sign in again first). The account, its devices,
  sessions, passkeys and sign-in methods are deleted at once, and your name is replaced with "Former member" in every
  workspace you belonged to. Your access requests are deleted with it. If you are the only owner of a workspace that
  has other members, make someone else an owner or delete the workspace first. <!-- lib/v2/account.ts deleteAccount -->
- **Everything else:** email [PRIVACY CONTACT EMAIL]. We answer within one month.
- **Workspace data:** ask the organization that owns the workspace; we will help them answer.

If you live in California, you have similar rights to know, delete and correct, and we do not sell or share your
personal information as California law defines those terms.

## International transfers

Hosted Align runs in the United States (Fly.io region `sjc`), and our subprocessors are in the United States. When we
transfer personal data from the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, we rely on the European Commission's 2021 Standard
Contractual Clauses, with the UK Addendum and the Swiss adjustments, as the [DPA](dpa.md) sets out.

## Security

How we protect data is described in our [security overview](security-overview.md).

## Children

Align is a tool for work. It is not meant for anyone under 16, and we do not knowingly collect their data. If you
think a child has given us personal data, write to [PRIVACY CONTACT EMAIL] and we will delete it.

## Changes to this policy

We will post any change here with a new date. If a change matters to how we use your data, we will tell account
holders by email before it takes effect.

## Contact

[LEGAL ENTITY]. Privacy questions and requests: [PRIVACY CONTACT EMAIL].

# Security overview

> Prepared 2026-10-30 from the code and configuration in this repository, for review before it is published. It says
> what Align does today and, at the end, what it does not do yet. [LEGAL ENTITY] publishes it. Report a security
> problem to [SECURITY CONTACT EMAIL].

Align keeps goals, who may change them, and the coding agents working toward them in step. It never needs to see
what people say to their agents: the server stores no prompt text, tool output, messages or code.

## In short

- One server on one Fly.io machine, behind Fly's HTTPS edge, with one SQLite database on a Fly volume that Fly
  encrypts at rest.
- No prompts, tool output, messages, code or file contents are stored on the server.
- People sign in as themselves: an emailed one-time code, Google, GitHub, or a passkey. There are no passwords.
- Sessions last 7 days from last use and never more than 30 days from sign-in. Sensitive actions need a sign-in from
  the last 15 minutes. "Sign out everywhere" ends every session at once.
- Every request is authorized in one policy module by workspace role, team role and goal visibility.
- Device, AI app and invite tokens are stored only as hashes. Refresh tokens rotate, and reusing an old one revokes
  the device or the app.
- Connected AI apps get read-only access to one workspace, as the person who connected them; adding evidence links
  needs a separate scope.
- Data is deleted on a published schedule ([retention](../RETENTION.md)), and an account can be deleted in the app.
- Local mode keeps everything on the person's own machine.
- Not yet: SOC 2, ISO 27001, a penetration test, SSO/SAML/SCIM. See "Not yet" below.

## Architecture

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Server | One Next.js process on one Fly.io machine (region `sjc`, San Jose, California), 1 CPU and 1 GB. A second server on the same data refuses to start. <!-- fly.toml; lib/startup.ts pid file --> |
| Edge | Fly's proxy terminates TLS and redirects plain HTTP to HTTPS. Align answers only for its own host names, only for requests that came through Fly's edge over HTTPS, and only on an allowlist of paths: everything else is 404, so a route added later stays closed until it is listed. <!-- fly.toml force_https; proxy.ts --> |
| Database | One SQLite file, `/data/v2/align.sqlite`, file mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, on a Fly volume. Fly states that volumes are created with encryption at rest by default; that is Fly's control, not Align's. <!-- lib/v2/db.ts; https://fly.io/docs/volumes/overview/ --> |
| Image | Built from an allowlisted context: no tests, docs, local agent packages or `.env` files reach the image. It runs as the unprivileged `node` user. <!-- Dockerfile; .dockerignore --> |
| Secrets | `ALIGN_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (32+ characters each), the email API key and any Google, GitHub or Turnstile secrets are set with `fly secrets`, never in the repository or the image. A server missing a required setting refuses to start. <!-- lib/config.ts; lib/v2/config.ts v2Problems --> |
| Outside services | Fly.io, the configured email API (Resend by default), Cloudflare Turnstile when enabled, and Google and GitHub for sign-in when configured. No AI model provider. See [subprocessors](subprocessors.md). |

## What Align stores, and what it does not

| Stored | Not stored |
| --- | --- |
| Account: email, name, profile picture address from Google or GitHub, linked sign-in methods, passkeys (public keys) | Passwords (there are none) |
| Workspace: members and roles, teams, invites, goals and their versions, alignments, change requests and decisions, directives | Prompt text, tool output, messages, code, file contents |
| Shared sessions: harness, a hashed repository key, an optional repository alias, times, state, goal binding, token usage and estimated cost | A session title: the `align` agent sends none <!-- docs/RETENTION.md --> |
| Work signals for 24 hours: keyed hashes of files touched; file paths and short text only if the person turns on "share work signals" | Anything from a session the person did not choose to share |
| Change request evidence: typed links (pull request, CI run, incident, dashboard, document or other) labelled self-reported or agent-reported, and a goal snapshot Align computes itself | Any claim that evidence is verified: Align labels it, it does not check it |
| Product events: an event name, the workspace, a keyed hash of the person, the time and a few allowlisted properties | Emails, names, titles, URLs or tokens in those events |
| Audit log: who did what to which object, and when | The content of goals or requests in the audit log |

## Signing in

- **Email one-time codes.** 6 digits, valid 5 minutes, 3 attempts, stored as a SHA-256 hash. Sends are limited
  per address and per client, durably when hosted (see "Rate limits"). The answer to a send never says whether an
  account exists. A code makes a new account only for a pending invite, an approved access request's creation code,
  or the server's first owner. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts -->
- **Google and GitHub.** Standard OAuth sign-in through Better Auth, asking only for identity (Google `openid`,
  `email`, `profile`; GitHub `read:user`, `user:email`). Accounts are linked only explicitly, from the account page,
  never by a matching email. An account whose email the provider did not verify can't be taken over with an email
  code. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts -->
- **Passkeys.** WebAuthn passkeys, added from the account page after a recent sign-in, with the public host as the
  relying party. Signing in with a passkey is phishing-resistant. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts passkey() -->
- **No passwords.** A password sign-in exists only as a local test switch, which a hosted server refuses to start
  with. <!-- lib/v2/config.ts v2Problems ALIGN_TEST_IDP -->
- **Sessions.** A random token in a signed `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie
  (`__Secure-align_v2.session_token`), kept in the database as Better Auth issues it.
  A session lasts 7 days, extended while it is used, and never more than 30 days after the sign-in that made it
  (`ALIGN_SESSION_MAX_DAYS`, 1 to 365). **Sign out everywhere** ends all of a person's sessions and can also unpair
  their devices and disconnect their AI apps. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts; lib/v2/account.ts signOutEverywhere -->
- **Recent sign-in for sensitive actions.** A sign-in from the last 15 minutes is needed to approve a device or an AI
  app, change a role, remove a member, invite an owner, delete or restore a workspace, add a passkey, link an
  account, sign out everywhere, and delete the account. <!-- lib/v2/config.ts RECENT_SIGN_IN_MS; requireRecentSignIn callers -->

Email codes alone are a single factor (NIST AAL1). People who want a phishing-resistant sign-in can add a passkey.

## Who may do what

- **Workspace roles.** Owners manage the workspace (invites, teams, roles, removal, deletion, the audit log);
  members create goals and share sessions; viewers read. **Team roles:** leads manage their team's members and team
  goals. <!-- lib/v2/policy.ts WORKSPACE_ROLE_ACTIONS, POD_ROLE_ACTIONS -->
- **Goal visibility.** Private (its owner only), team, or workspace. A workspace owner does not read others' private
  goals. <!-- lib/v2/policy.ts -->
- **One decision point.** Every route asks the same policy module. Something the caller may not see answers 404, so
  its existence does not leak; something visible but not allowed answers 403. <!-- lib/v2/policy.ts -->
- **Leaving.** When a person leaves or is removed, their access ends at once: team places, device access and
  connected AI apps for that workspace. <!-- lib/v2/lifecycle.ts -->

## Tokens and keys

| Credential | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Device pairing (the `align` CLI) | A device makes an Ed25519 key pair and a person approves its code in the browser after a recent sign-in. Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 30 days, rotate on every use, and each refresh is signed with the device's private key. Presenting a refresh token that was already used revokes the device. Only SHA-256 hashes of tokens are stored. <!-- lib/v2/devices.ts --> |
| Connected AI apps (OAuth 2.1) | Authorization code with PKCE (S256) only, public clients, refresh token rotation, resource binding. A person approves one app for one workspace after a recent sign-in. Access tokens last 1 hour and are checked against the grant and the person's membership on every call. Refresh tokens last 7 days from the grant and are never extended; reusing an old one deletes the grant. Refresh tokens are stored only as keyed hashes. <!-- lib/oauth/server.ts; lib/oauth/grants.ts --> |
| What an app may do | Read only, through nine tools: goals, a goal, change requests, decision records, directives, goal limits, asks between teams, agent activity counts toward goals and a short brief. An app may add agent-reported evidence links to change requests through a tenth tool only if the person grants the separate `changes:evidence` scope, and each grant records the scopes it was given. <!-- lib/mcp/register.ts --> |
| Invite links, device pairing secrets, creation codes | Stored only as hashes (creation codes as an HMAC under `ALIGN_SECRET`). <!-- lib/v2/db.ts token_hash, device_code_hash, code_hash --> |
| Server secrets | Rotating `ALIGN_SECRET` ends every connected app and unused creation code; rotating `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` signs everyone out. <!-- lib/secret.ts; docs/HOSTING.md --> |
| Google and GitHub tokens | Better Auth keeps the access and refresh tokens the provider issued at sign-in or linking in the database, encrypted (XChaCha20-Poly1305 under the server's `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`). An ID token (Google issues one: a signed, short-lived statement of who signed in) is stored as issued. Align does not use these tokens after sign-in, and no route returns them: Better Auth's routes that would hand out, refresh or describe them (and the one that unlinks a provider) are turned off. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts account.encryptOAuthTokens, DISABLED_PATHS --> |

## Requests from browsers and AI apps

- A write made with the sign-in cookie must carry this server's exact `Origin`, so another site can't make one.
  <!-- lib/v2/http.ts -->
- Device and MCP routes refuse requests from browsers. <!-- lib/v2/http.ts; specs/align/mcp.md -->
- The AI app consent page can't be framed, cached or leaked in a `Referer`. <!-- next.config.ts -->
- Text written by people comes back to AI apps marked as untrusted, so an agent can tell data from instructions.
  <!-- lib/mcp/register.ts -->
- Align sends agents only facts and an enforced stop: no free-text instructions, and nothing wakes an idle agent.
- When Align fetches an AI app's client document, it refuses private network addresses, limits size and time, and
  caches the result. <!-- lib/oauth/clients.ts -->

## Rate limits and abuse controls

- Email-code sends: 3 per address per 10 minutes, 10 per client per hour, and, hosted, 5 per address per hour and
  3 per client per minute, counted in the database so a restart doesn't reset them. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts -->
- Better Auth's own limits on sign-in routes when hosted, also counted in the database. <!-- lib/v2/auth.ts rateLimit -->
- Limits on workspace creation, invites, device pairing and device-code lookups. <!-- specs/align/workspaces.md -->
- Hosted workspace creation needs a single-use creation code by default, and the operator can close creation
  entirely. Caps on workspaces (100), workspaces per person (2), members per workspace (25) and new shared sessions
  per device per day (500), each configurable. <!-- lib/v2/config.ts caps(), creationMode() -->
- Disposable email domains can't request access or create a workspace. <!-- lib/v2/disposable.ts -->
- Cloudflare Turnstile on email-code sign-in, access requests and workspace creation, when its keys are set. A
  hosted server without them starts and logs a warning. <!-- lib/v2/captcha.ts; lib/startup.ts -->

## Logging and the audit log

- When hosted, the server logs no request body, path, address, email or code. A server error logs only the error's
  name. Email failures log only the HTTP status. The retention job logs counts only. <!-- lib/v2/http.ts; lib/v2/core.mts postEmail; lib/v2/retention.ts -->
- Fly.io keeps the machine's log output on its platform for a limited time; Align keeps no copy.
- Each workspace has an audit log of who did what to which object, and when: membership and roles, invites, teams,
  goal versions, change requests and alignments and their decisions, devices, connected apps, passkeys, stopped
  agents, deletions and restores. Owners can read it. It is kept 1 year. A change request approved without evidence
  is recorded as such. <!-- lib/v2/db.ts v2_audit; docs/RETENTION.md -->
- Content-free product events are kept 13 months and are visible to the operator only.

## Backups and recovery

- Fly.io takes a daily snapshot of the volume, kept 7 days. <!-- fly.toml scheduled_snapshots, snapshot_retention = 7 -->
- Align makes no other backup, off-site or otherwise. Restoring from a snapshot would lose the changes since it was
  taken, up to a day.
- One machine in one region: if it fails, Align is down until it is restored. There is no standby.
- Fly checks the server's health every 30 seconds. <!-- fly.toml http_service.checks -->

## Deletion and retention

The full schedule is [RETENTION.md](../RETENTION.md). In short: shared session rows are rolled up without the person
after 13 months; the audit log is kept 1 year; removed members are shown as "Former member" after 30 days; a deleted
workspace can be restored for 30 days and is then purged, and is gone from every snapshot within 38 days; an account
deleted in the app is deleted at once. Approved and declined access requests are deleted 13 months after the
decision, pending ones 13 months after they were made. Product events are kept 13 months.

## Local mode

Align also runs on a person's own machine (Mode L). The database stays in `data/v2/align.sqlite` there and nothing is
sent to [LEGAL ENTITY]. The local server answers only to loopback host names, so another website can't reach it under
its own name. It prints sign-in codes instead of emailing them. It reaches the internet only for Google or GitHub
sign-in, if configured, and to read the client document of an AI app the person connects. <!-- proxy.ts; lib/v2/mail.ts -->

## How the code is made

- The code is in git. Dependencies are locked with `package-lock.json`, and the sign-in library (Better Auth and its
  passkey plugin) is pinned to an exact version. <!-- package.json -->
- Integration tests start real servers and cover sign-in, authorization, the hosted edge, connected apps and the
  retention job (`scripts/test-v2.mjs`, `scripts/test-oauth.mjs`), and the hosted image has its own test
  (`scripts/test-image.sh`). They are run by developers; no CI service runs them yet.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Email [SECURITY CONTACT EMAIL]. See `SECURITY.md` in the repository for what to include and what to expect.

## Not yet

These are not in place. Each is available to discuss for a specific customer.

- No SOC 2 report and no ISO 27001 certification.
- No independent penetration test.
- No SSO (SAML or OIDC) and no SCIM provisioning. Available on request.
- No per-workspace settings for session length or retention.
- No customer-managed keys, and no encryption of the database beyond Fly's volume encryption, except Google and
  GitHub access and refresh tokens, which are encrypted.
- Browser session tokens are stored as issued, not hashed, and so is a Google ID token.
- No off-site backups, no standby machine, and one region.
- No site-wide Content-Security-Policy or HSTS header yet (the consent page has its own framing protections).
- No automated dependency or secret scanning in CI, and no CI test run.
- No bug bounty.
- No written incident-response runbook; the commitment to customers is in the [DPA](dpa.md): notice within 72 hours.

# Subprocessors

> Draft for counsel review, prepared 2026-10-30. It lists the services hosted Align uses to process personal data, as
> the code and configuration in this repository set them up. [LEGAL ENTITY] publishes it; questions go to
> [PRIVACY CONTACT EMAIL].

A subprocessor is a company that processes personal data for Align when Align processes data for a customer. This page
covers hosted Align only. Align in local mode (Mode L) runs on your own machine, and Align sends nothing from it to
anyone (see "Local mode" below).

## Subprocessors

| Subprocessor | What it does for Align | Personal data it processes | Location | When it is used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fly.io, Inc. | Hosting: runs Align's one server, stores its database on an encrypted volume with daily snapshots kept 7 days, terminates HTTPS at its edge, and keeps the machine's log output | Everything hosted Align stores (see the privacy policy) | United States: region `sjc`, San Jose, California | Always, when hosted <!-- fly.toml: primary_region = "sjc", [[mounts]] snapshot_retention = 7 --> |
| The configured email API: Resend in the default configuration | Sends sign-in codes and creation-code messages | The recipient's email address and the message: a sign-in code and link, or a creation code with the recipient's name | United States | When the email settings are set (`ALIGN_EMAIL_API_URL`, `ALIGN_EMAIL_API_KEY`, `ALIGN_EMAIL_FROM`); the default configuration points at `https://api.resend.com/emails` <!-- fly.toml; lib/v2/core.mts postEmail --> |
| Cloudflare, Inc. (Turnstile) | The check that a visitor is a person, on email-code sign-in, access requests and workspace creation | What the Turnstile widget collects in the browser, the token it issues, and the visitor's IP address, which Align passes with the token | Global network; Cloudflare, Inc. is in the United States | Only when both `ALIGN_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` and `ALIGN_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` are set <!-- lib/v2/config.ts turnstile(); lib/v2/captcha.ts sends remoteip from Fly-Client-IP --> |

## Authentication providers

Google and GitHub are used for sign-in only, and only when a person chooses them. Align asks each for the person's
identity and nothing more: Google for `openid`, `email` and `profile`; GitHub for `read:user` and `user:email`
(Better Auth's default scopes). Align receives a name, an email address, a profile picture address and the
provider's account id. It reads no other data from either service.

| Provider | Used for | Hosts the server calls | When it is used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google LLC | "Continue with Google" | `accounts.google.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, `www.googleapis.com` | Only when `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are set <!-- lib/v2/config.ts googleConfigured; @better-auth/core social-providers/google --> |
| GitHub, Inc. | "Continue with GitHub" | `github.com`, `api.github.com` | Only when `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` are set <!-- lib/v2/config.ts githubConfigured; @better-auth/core social-providers/github --> |

## Not subprocessors

- **AI model providers.** Align's server calls no AI model: not Anthropic, not OpenAI, not any other. It sends no
  workspace data to one, and it trains no model. <!-- no model-provider host anywhere in app/, lib/ or proxy.ts; test-v2 checks -->
- **AI apps you connect.** When a person connects an AI app (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex) to Align, the app
  reads one workspace through Align's MCP endpoint, as that person and with their permissions. The app is that
  person's or their organization's own tool, under their own agreement with its maker, not a service Align uses.
  To learn an app's name and its allowed return addresses, Align fetches the app's public client document from the
  address the app gives (for Claude, an address on `claude.ai`). That request carries no personal data.
  <!-- lib/oauth/clients.ts CIMD; specs/align/mcp.md -->
- **Font hosting.** Align's fonts are downloaded when the app is built and served from Align's own address, so a
  page view sends nothing to a font service. <!-- app/layout.tsx next/font/google self-hosts at build -->
- **Analytics.** Align uses no third-party analytics, tracking or advertising service. Its product funnel events are
  counted in its own database.

## Every external host the hosted server can call

| Host | Who | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Local mode

In local mode the database stays in `data/v2/align.sqlite` on the person's own machine. Sign-in codes are printed on
that machine, not emailed, and the bot check is off. The local server reaches the internet only to sign in with
Google or GitHub, if the person configured them, and to read the client document of an AI app the person connects.
[LEGAL ENTITY] receives nothing from a local server. <!-- lib/v2/mail.ts; lib/v2/config.ts turnstile() is hosted only -->

## Annex II: Technical and organizational measures

A summary of the [security overview](security-overview.md):

- **Encryption.** HTTPS at the hosting provider's edge; the database volume is encrypted at rest by the hosting
  provider.
- **Access control.** People sign in individually (email codes, Google, GitHub or passkeys; no passwords). Sessions
  last 7 days from last use and at most 30 days. Sensitive actions require a sign-in from the last 15 minutes. Every
  request is authorized by workspace role, team role and goal visibility.
- **Credentials.** Device, AI app and invite tokens are stored as hashes; refresh tokens rotate and reuse revokes them; devices hold their own
  keys; connected AI apps are read-only and limited to one workspace, except for adding agent-reported evidence links
  with the separate `changes:evidence` scope.
- **Data minimization.** No prompts, agent output or code on the server.
- **Abuse prevention.** Rate limits, creation codes and caps, a disposable-domain block, and a bot check.
- **Logging.** A per-workspace audit log kept 1 year; server logs hold no request bodies, addresses, emails or codes.
- **Availability.** Daily volume snapshots kept 7 days and a health check every 30 seconds.
- **Deletion.** A published retention schedule applied by a daily job, and in-app deletion of accounts and
  workspaces.
- **Subprocessors.** A published list with 30 days' notice of changes.

# How long Align keeps data

This is Align's published retention schedule. It describes what the code does: the retention job in
`lib/v2/retention.ts`, account deletion in `lib/v2/account.ts`, workspace deletion in `lib/v2/workspaces.ts`, and the
volume snapshots in `fly.toml`. The contract is the "Data retention" requirement in `specs/align/workspaces.md`.

Align never stores prompt text, tool output or messages on the server. The `align` agent shares a session's harness, a
hashed repository key, an optional repository alias, its times and state, its goal binding and its token usage and
estimated cost. It sends no title.

## The schedule

| Data | Kept | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt text, tool output, messages | Not stored on the server | Nothing to delete |
| Shared sessions: harness, hashed repo key, repo alias, times, state, goal binding, binding periods, usage (model, tokens, estimated cost), the person who shared it | 13 months after the session ends: when sharing stopped, or else its last activity (its last upload, binding change or update) | Rolled up into totals per workspace, goal, UTC day, model and billing basis, with no person and no session. The raw rows (session, binding periods, usage, directive deliveries and receipts) are deleted |
| Change-request evidence links (kind, URL, label, who added it, person or agent) and the snapshot Align records with each revision (the goal's 30-day spend, bound sessions, last activity) | The life of the change request | Deleted with the workspace. Whoever added a link becomes "Former member #n" like the rest of their rows |
| Asks between teams (the team asked, the text, who asked as people said it, the meeting and date, who recorded and last decided it) and the times they came up again | Open and accepted ones while the workspace lives; a `done`, `declined` or `withdrawn` ask 13 months after its last change | Deleted by the daily job, with the times it came up again (`asks_deleted`), or with the workspace. Whoever recorded, decided or mentioned one becomes "Former member #n" like the rest of their rows |
| Value reports on an approved change request (an estimate and an optional note of up to 500 characters, by one person) | 13 months after their last change | Deleted by the daily job (`value_reports_deleted`), with their change request, or with the workspace. Their author becomes "Former member #n" like the rest of their rows |
| Requests to a goal's agents (type, goal and version, target goal, an optional note of up to 280 characters, who sent and cancelled it) and each session's answer | 13 months after it was sent | Deleted by the daily job (`requests_deleted`) with the directives that carried it, with their session (that session's answer), or with the workspace. Its sender becomes "Former member #n" like the rest of their rows |
| The marker a deleted session's shared history leaves (a hash of the person who shared it and the session key, the workspace, the time; never the key or the person) | 13 months after the deletion | Deleted by the daily job (`deleted_session_markers_deleted`), or with the workspace. While it lasts, the account that shared the session is told its history is already deleted (410 `history_deleted`) when one of its devices asks to delete it again |
| Goal holds (who held the goal, an optional reason of up to 280 characters, when) | While the goal is held | Deleted when it is released (by a person, or when the goal is achieved or dropped) or with the workspace; the audit log keeps the history. Whoever held it becomes "Former member #n" like the rest of their rows |
| Spend roll-ups (no person, no session) | The life of the workspace | Deleted with the workspace |
| Activity signals (in-flight edits, commits, tasks, claims) | 24 hours (claims 1 hour) | Deleted by the daily job, or with their session |
| Workspace audit log | 1 year | Deleted |
| A person who leaves or is removed | Their access ends at once: team places, device access and connected AI apps for that workspace. Their goals, sessions and history stay under their name for 30 days | After 30 days they are shown as "Former member #n" (numbered per workspace) in every row of that workspace, the audit log included; their sessions no longer point at their device, invites to or accepted by them are deleted, so their email leaves the workspace, and the keyed hash that stood for them is cleared from that workspace's product events. Their account stays until they delete it |
| Sessions of a removed member, if the owner ticks "Also delete their shared sessions in this workspace now" | Deleted at removal | Spend already rolled up stays |
| An account, when its owner deletes it (`/app/account`) | Deleted at once | Their memberships end as above, and in every workspace their rows become "Former member #n" at once. Their product events lose the keyed hash that stood for them. Their devices, sign-in sessions, linked sign-in methods, passkeys (with when each was last used), their answer to the "add a passkey" prompt, codes, access requests, unused creation codes bound to their email, email-keyed rate-limit counters and the account are deleted. A workspace where they were the only member is deleted with it (see the next row). The audit records that an account was deleted, with no name or email. Refused while they are the only owner of a workspace that has other members |
| A deleted workspace (by an owner, with the account of its only member, or by the operator) | 30 days, during which its owners can restore it from Your workspaces | Every row is deleted by the daily job on day 30 or within the 24 hours after, its audit included (its content-free product events stay, under a random id, until their own 13 months are up). The operator can erase one at once (`align-admin workspaces delete <ws> --purge --yes`) |
| Fly.io volume snapshots (hosted) | Daily snapshots, each kept 7 days (`fly.toml`: `scheduled_snapshots = true`, `snapshot_retention = 7`) | Expire, so deleted data leaves the snapshots within 7 days. A purged workspace is gone from every copy within 38 days of its deletion |
| Off-site backups | None are made | |
| Email sign-in codes | 5 minutes, 3 attempts | Deleted by the daily job once expired |
| Sign-in sessions (with the client IP address and user agent when hosted) | 7 days, extended while used, and never more than 30 days after the sign-in (`ALIGN_SESSION_MAX_DAYS`). Signing out everywhere ends them all at once | A session past the 30 days is deleted when it is next presented; the daily job deletes the rest once expired or past the 30 days |
| Pending invites | 7 days | Deleted 7 days after they expire. An accepted invite is kept while the person is a member, and deleted when they become a former member or with the workspace |
| Passkeys (name, public key, when added and last used) | Until the person deletes the passkey | Deleted at once, or with the account |
| Access requests (`/app/request-access`: email, name, company, team size, what for, interest) | 13 months after the operator approved or declined it, or, while still pending, 13 months after it was made | Deleted by the daily job, or at once when that email's Align account is deleted |
| Creation codes (an HMAC of the code, the email it is bound to, dates, the workspace it created) | Kept as the record of who could create what | An unused code bound to an account's email is deleted with that account; a used one then keeps no email or redeemer. Purging a workspace clears the code's workspace |
| Product events (`v2_events`: an event name such as "workspace created" or "first session bound to a goal", the workspace id, a keyed hash of the person, the time, and a few allowlisted kinds or counts; never an email, name, title, goal text, URL, repository, code or token) | 13 months | Deleted by the daily job. When a person deletes their account, their keyed hash is cleared from every event at once, so no event can be tied to them (the event itself stays, without a person). When a workspace is purged, its events stay with its id replaced by a random one (`wsx_…`) that names nothing. When a person who left or was removed becomes "Former member #n" in a workspace (30 days on), their hash is cleared from that workspace's events the same way |
| Durable rate-limit counters (an HMAC of an email address or a client address, and a time) | 24 hours | Pruned as new calls are counted; the ones keyed by an account's email are deleted with the account |
| Paired devices (name, public key, last seen) | Until the person revokes the device; a revoked device's row stays, without working tokens | Deleted with the account |
| AI apps that registered themselves (`_oauth_clients.json`: an app's name and redirect addresses, nothing about people) | Kept | |
| Server logs | When hosted, Align logs no request body, path, address, email or code; a server error logs only its error name, and the retention job logs counts only | Fly.io keeps a machine's log output on its platform for a limited time; Align keeps no copy |
| Email provider message logs | The provider's own retention (set it to the shortest it offers) | The provider deletes them |
| Local mode (Mode L) | Everything stays in `data/v2/align.sqlite` on the person's own machine; nothing is sent to Align | The same job runs there, on that machine |

## When the job runs

- At every server start, and then every 24 hours while the server runs (`instrumentation.ts`). It never runs during a
  build.
- By hand, with the operator script: `node scripts/align-admin.mjs retention run` runs it now and prints what it did;
  `--dry-run` prints what it would do and changes nothing (`node scripts/retention.mjs [--dry-run]` is the same
  command). It reads `ALIGN_DATA_DIR` (default `./data`) and runs the same code as the server
  (`lib/v2/retention-core.mts`). Run it with the server's environment, because it reads `ALIGN_SESSION_MAX_DAYS` the
  way the server does: on the hosted machine, `fly ssh console -C "node scripts/align-admin.mjs retention run"` (the
  image carries the script) has that environment.
- The operator can also erase one workspace at once, without waiting for its restore window:
  `node scripts/align-admin.mjs workspaces delete <ws> --purge --yes`, the same purge the job does on day 30.
- Each step is its own short transaction and running the job again changes nothing.

Deleted data can't be recovered by Align once the job has removed it: Align keeps no other copy than the volume
snapshots above.
